**Working Document 05 — WKSPSIM 2026**

**Stock:** Anchovy (*Engraulis encrasicolus*) in the southern part of Division 9.a  
(Gulf of Cadiz and southern part of Portugal), ane.27.9aS

**Affiliation:** Instituto Español de Oceanografía (IEO-CSIC), Centro Oceanográfico de Cádiz, Spain




```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(knitr)
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

fig_dir <- here("outputs","assessment_error","figures")
tab_dir <- here("outputs","assessment_error","tables")
rds_dir <- here("data","Rdata")

# Reproducible tabular outputs used by inline R expressions.
# They must be loaded in setup because inline expressions are evaluated
# before the later table chunks in which the same files are displayed.
assessment_parameters <- read.csv(
  file.path(tab_dir,"01_assessment_error_parameters.csv"),
  check.names=FALSE
)

assessment_temporal <- read.csv(
  file.path(tab_dir,"02_assessment_error_temporal_structure.csv")
)

emulator_validation <- read.csv(
  file.path(tab_dir,"03_emulator_validation.csv")
)

assessment_par_rds <- readRDS(
  file.path(rds_dir,"assessment_error_parameters.rds")
)

assessment_revisions_rds <- readRDS(
  file.path(rds_dir,"assessment_error_historical_revisions.rds")
)

emulator_reference_rds <- readRDS(
  file.path(rds_dir,"assessment_error_simulated_reference.rds")
)

assessment_error_reference <- readRDS(
  file.path(rds_dir,"assessment_error_reference_1000iter.rds")
)

variables <- c("SSB","F","R")

error_wide_wd <- assessment_revisions_rds %>%
  dplyr::select(update_year,variable,log_error) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from=variable,values_from=log_error) %>%
  tidyr::drop_na(dplyr::all_of(variables)) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(update_year)

ssb_f_loo_wd <- lapply(error_wide_wd$update_year,function(y) {
  x <- dplyr::filter(error_wide_wd,update_year!=y)
  data.frame(
    omitted_year=y,
    Pearson=cor(x$SSB,x$F,method="pearson"),
    Spearman=cor(x$SSB,x$F,method="spearman")
  )
}) %>%
  dplyr::bind_rows()

ssb_f_loo_summary_wd <- ssb_f_loo_wd %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    Pearson_min=min(Pearson),
    Pearson_max=max(Pearson),
    Spearman_min=min(Spearman),
    Spearman_max=max(Spearman)
  )

emulator_cor_wd <- cor(emulator_reference_rds[,variables])

ae_multiplier <- assessment_error_reference$multiplier
ae_log_multiplier <- log(ae_multiplier)
ae_generated_mean <- apply(ae_log_multiplier,3,mean)
ae_generated_sd <- apply(ae_log_multiplier,3,sd)
ae_generated_cor <- cor(
  matrix(
    ae_log_multiplier,
    ncol=3,
    dimnames=list(NULL,variable=dimnames(ae_multiplier)$variable)
  )
)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo=FALSE,
  warning=FALSE,
  message=FALSE,
  fig.align="center"
)

  tab <- knitr::kable(
    x,
    format="latex",
    booktabs=TRUE,
    digits=digits,
    align=align,
    caption=NULL
  )

  cat("\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n")

  cat("\\label{",label,"}\n",sep="")
  cat("\\",font_size,"\n",sep="")
  cat("\\begin{adjustbox}{max width=\\textwidth}\n")
  cat(tab)
  cat("\n\\end{adjustbox}\n")
  cat("\\end{table}\n")
}

# General approach

Management Strategy Evaluation (MSE) uses closed-loop simulations to represent
population dynamics, the perception of stock status, and the implementation of
management measures [@Punt2016].

In a full MSE, the assessment model can be run during each management cycle
using data generated by the Operating Model (OM). In the *shortcut MSE*
developed for Gulf of Cadiz anchovy (*Engraulis encrasicolus*, ane.27.9aS),
Stock Synthesis 3 (SS3) is not refitted during the projection. Assessment
uncertainty is represented by a statistical emulator that introduces error
into the perception of the stock quantities used by the management procedure
[@Wiedenmann2015; @ICES2020].

The simulation cycle therefore distinguishes between the population state
represented by the OM and the perceived state used by the management
procedure:

\[
\text{Operating Model}
\longrightarrow
\text{assessment-error emulator}
\longrightarrow
\text{Management Procedure}
\longrightarrow
\text{management action}
\longrightarrow
\text{Operating Model}.
\]

Assessment uncertainty is kept separate from the uncertainty used to
condition the OM. The 100 OMs represent alternative population conditions
derived from historical conditioning, whereas *assessment error* represents
error in the perception of those conditions during the projection.

The emulator was parameterized from historical revisions of the SS3
assessment for ane.27.9aS. These revisions were used to estimate bias,
variability, correlation among variables, and temporal dependence of
assessment error.

The *assessment error* was parameterized jointly for spawning-stock biomass
(SSB), fishing mortality (\(F\)), and recruitment (\(R\)). All three
variables are retained in the assessment-error object. The reference MP
documented in WD06 uses the SSB and F multipliers, whereas recruitment
assessment error remains disabled.

This WD05 documents the parameterization and validation of the assessment
error used in the *shortcut MSE*. WD06 documents its incorporation into the
perceived state used by the MP, and subsequent WDs evaluate its consequences
for management-procedure performance.


# Methods {#methods}

## Historical characterization of *assessment error* {#historical-ae}

### SS3 assessments used

The *assessment error* was parameterized from a sequence of SS3 assessments
with terminal years from 2004 to 2024. The assessments used the same model
configuration and differed in terminal year.

For each run, convergence was checked using the maximum gradient reported by
SS3. Runs satisfying the following criterion were included:

\[
\text{max gradient}<0.001.
\]

Positive and finite estimates of spawning-stock biomass (SSB), fishing
mortality (\(F\)), and recruitment (\(R\)) were used to calculate
*assessment error*.

The sequence provided 20 annual updates for the period 2005--2024.

### Annual revisions

For each variable \(X\) and update year \(t\), the estimate for year
\(t-1\) obtained from the assessment with terminal year \(t-1\) was compared
with the estimate for the same year obtained from the assessment with terminal
year \(t\):

\[
e_{X,t}
=
\log
\left(
\frac{\hat X_{t-1}^{(t-1)}}
     {\hat X_{t-1}^{(t)}}
\right),
\]

where \(\hat X_{t-1}^{(t-1)}\) is the estimate available before incorporating
the new year of information and \(\hat X_{t-1}^{(t)}\) is the revised
estimate after incorporating it.

The relative revision was also calculated:

\[
r_{X,t}
=
\frac{\hat X_{t-1}^{(t-1)}}
     {\hat X_{t-1}^{(t)}}-1.
\]

With this definition, positive values indicate that the previous estimate was
higher than the revised estimate, whereas negative values indicate that it was
lower.

The revisions were used as a proxy for assessment error. They do not
represent differences from the true stock state, which is unobserved. Their
use allows characterization of changes in estimates resulting from the
incorporation of additional information into the assessment
[@Mohn1999; @HurtadoFerro2015].

### Error parameterization

For each update, the log revisions of SSB, \(F\), and \(R\) were arranged
in the vector

\[
\mathbf e_t=
\begin{pmatrix}
e_{\mathrm{SSB},t}\\
e_{F,t}\\
e_{R,t}
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

From the \(n=20\) vectors, the mean vector was estimated as

\[
\boldsymbol{\mu}
=
\frac{1}{n}
\sum_{t=1}^{n}\mathbf e_t
\]

and the variance--covariance matrix as

\[
\boldsymbol{\Sigma}
=
\operatorname{Cov}(\mathbf e_t).
\]

The empirical mean was retained in the parameterization and the following
correction was not applied:

\[
-\frac{\sigma_X^2}{2}.
\]

Therefore, the multipliers generated from the log revisions retain the mean
bias estimated from the historical revisions and are not adjusted to impose
an expectation equal to one on the multiplicative scale.

The full \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}\) matrix was used, retaining the estimated
covariation among the revisions of SSB, \(F\), and \(R\).

The stability of the relationship between SSB and \(F\) revisions was
examined using a *leave-one-year-out* analysis. For each update year, the
corresponding vector was removed and Pearson and Spearman correlations between
the two variables were recalculated.

### Temporal structure

Temporal dependence of the revisions was evaluated separately for SSB,
\(F\), and \(R\) using

\[
e_{X,t}
=
\alpha_X+
\phi_X e_{X,t-1}
+
\varepsilon_{X,t}.
\]

For each variable, the first-order coefficient \(\phi_X\) and its
\(p\)-value were estimated. These results were used to define the temporal
dependence of assessment error in the reference scenario.

## *Assessment-error* emulator {#ae-emulator}

In the *shortcut MSE*, SS3 is not refitted during each annual management
cycle. Assessment uncertainty is represented by a statistical emulator
parameterized from the historical revisions described in Section
\@ref(historical-ae).

For each year \(t\), the reference model generates

\[
\mathbf e_t
\overset{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}
\mathcal{N}_3
\left(
\boldsymbol{\mu},
\boldsymbol{\Sigma}
\right).
\]

Independence is assumed among years, whereas dependence among SSB, \(F\),
and \(R\) within each year is determined by \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}\).

For each variable \(X\), the error is transformed to the multiplicative scale as

\[
M_{X,t}
=
\exp(e_{X,t}).
\]

During the *closed-loop* simulation, perceived quantities are obtained as

\[
X^{\mathrm{perc}}_t
=
X^{\mathrm{true}}_t M_{X,t},
\]

where \(X^{\mathrm{true}}_t\) is the state generated by the OM and
\(X^{\mathrm{perc}}_t\) is the perceived state used by the management
procedure.

This WD parameterizes and validates the *assessment-error* generator. The
application of the multipliers to the perceived state and their propagation
to management advice are subsequently checked with the Management Procedure
\(F_{cap}+B_{esc}\).

## Emulator validation {#ae-validation}

### Internal validation

The implementation of the multivariate model was checked using 10,000
independent realizations:

\[
\mathbf e_s
\sim
\mathcal{N}_3
\left(
\boldsymbol{\mu},
\boldsymbol{\Sigma}
\right),
\qquad s=1,\ldots,10000.
\]

A fixed seed (`set.seed(123)`) was used. For each variable, the mean and
standard deviation of the realizations were calculated together with the
correlation matrix among variables. These statistics were compared with the
\(\boldsymbol{\mu}\) vector, the standard deviations derived from
\(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}\), and the correlation matrix used to parameterize
the emulator.

This check evaluates whether the generator reproduces the specified moments
and correlation structure. It does not evaluate the assumption of
multivariate normality of the historical revisions.

Five temporal sequences were additionally generated as a graphical diagnostic
of the reference process. These sequences are not part of the 1,000
realizations subsequently used in the MSE.

### Validation using conventional retrospectives {#external-validation}

Validation using information not used in the parameterization was conducted
with conventional SS3 retrospectives corresponding to *peels* -1 to -5.
These runs were not used to estimate \(\boldsymbol{\mu}\) or
\(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}\).

For each variable \(X\) and *peel* \(k\), the observed retrospective error
was calculated as

\[
E^{\mathrm{obs}}_{X,k}
=
\log
\left(
\frac{\hat X^{(-k)}_{Y-k}}
     {\hat X^{(0)}_{Y-k}}
\right),
\]

where \(Y\) is the terminal year of the full assessment,
\(\hat X^{(-k)}_{Y-k}\) is the terminal estimate from retrospective
*peel* \(k\), and \(\hat X^{(0)}_{Y-k}\) is the estimate for the same year
in the full assessment.

Because a \(k\)-year *peel* represents the accumulation of \(k\) annual
updates, the simulated retrospective error was calculated as

\[
E^{\mathrm{sim}}_{X,k}
=
\sum_{j=1}^{k}e_{X,j}.
\]

Ten thousand sequences of five annual errors were generated. For each
variable and *peel*, the median and 5th and 95th percentiles of
\(E^{\mathrm{sim}}_{X,k}\) were calculated, and the observed retrospective
error was compared with this distribution.

As a second diagnostic, Mohn's rho was calculated [@Mohn1999]:

\[
\rho_X
=
\frac{1}{K}
\sum_{k=1}^{K}
\left[
\frac{\hat X^{(-k)}_{Y-k}}
     {\hat X^{(0)}_{Y-k}}
-1
\right],
\]

con \(K=5\).

The same statistic was calculated for each simulated sequence. For each
variable, the median and 5th and 95th percentiles of the simulated
distribution of \(\rho_X\) were obtained and compared with the observed
value. Mohn's rho was used to characterize the retrospective pattern and not
as an estimate of error relative to the true population state
[@Mohn1999; @HurtadoFerro2015].

As a third diagnostic, persistence in the sign of retrospective errors was
evaluated. For each variable, the number of *peels* with positive and negative
errors was counted. The same calculation was performed for each simulated
sequence, and the frequency with which the observed directional pattern
appeared in the simulations was estimated.

## Generation of realizations used in the MSE {#closed-loop-ae}

Once the emulator had been parameterized and validated, the *assessment-error*
realizations subsequently used in the MSE were generated.

For each year \(t\) and iteration \(i\),

\[
\mathbf e_{t,i}
\overset{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}
\mathcal{N}_3
\left(
\boldsymbol{\mu},
\boldsymbol{\Sigma}
\right),
\]

and the multipliers were calculated as

\[
\mathbf M_{t,i}
=
\exp(\mathbf e_{t,i}).
\]

Generation used a fixed seed (`set.seed(123)`) and produced 1,000
realizations for assessment years 2024--2053. The resulting object has
dimensions

\[
30\ \text{años}
\times
1000\ \text{iteraciones}
\times
3\ \text{variables}.
\]

Before saving the object, it was checked that its dimensions matched the
specified configuration, that the variables were SSB, \(F\), and \(R\),
and that all multipliers were finite and positive.

As a check of the final generation, the multipliers were transformed back to
the logarithmic scale and their means, standard deviations, and correlations
were calculated. These statistics were compared with \(\boldsymbol{\mu}\),
the standard deviations, and the correlation matrix used to parameterize the
emulator.

The subsequent application of the multipliers is defined as

\[
X^{\mathrm{perc}}_{t,i}
=
X^{\mathrm{true}}_{t,i}
M_{X,t,i}.
\]

This transformation is neither applied nor validated in this WD. Its
implementation on the perceived state used by the Management Procedure is
documented in WD06.


# Results {#results}

## Historical revisions and parameterization {#results-parameterisation}

Twenty annual revision vectors were obtained for SSB, \(F\), and recruitment,
corresponding to SS3 assessment updates between 2005 and 2024. The trajectories
of the assessments used to calculate the revisions are shown in Figure
\@ref(fig:fig-assessment-trajectories).

```{r fig-assessment-trajectories, out.width="75%", fig.cap="Trajectories of the SS3 assessments used to calculate annual revisions. Each line corresponds to an assessment with a terminal year between 2004 and 2024."}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(fig_dir,"01_historical_assessment_trajectories.png"))
```

The mean log revisions were
`r sprintf("%.3f",assessment_par_rds$mu["SSB"])` para SSB,
`r sprintf("%.3f",assessment_par_rds$mu["F"])` para \(F\) y
`r sprintf("%.3f",assessment_par_rds$mu["R"])` for recruitment. The
standard deviations were
`r sprintf("%.3f",sqrt(diag(assessment_par_rds$Sigma))["SSB"])`,
`r sprintf("%.3f",sqrt(diag(assessment_par_rds$Sigma))["F"])` y
`r sprintf("%.3f",sqrt(diag(assessment_par_rds$Sigma))["R"])`,
respectively (Table \@ref(tab:assessment-parameters)).
The correlations among log revisions were
`r sprintf("%.3f",assessment_par_rds$correlation["SSB","F"])` para SSB--\(F\),
`r sprintf("%.3f",assessment_par_rds$correlation["SSB","R"])` para SSB--\(R\)
y `r sprintf("%.3f",assessment_par_rds$correlation["F","R"])` para \(F\)--\(R\)
(Tabla \@ref(tab:assessment-parameters)).
In the leave-one-year-out analysis, the SSB--\(F\) correlation ranged from
`r sprintf("%.3f",ssb_f_loo_summary_wd$Pearson_min)` y
`r sprintf("%.3f",ssb_f_loo_summary_wd$Pearson_max)` for Pearson, and from
`r sprintf("%.3f",ssb_f_loo_summary_wd$Spearman_min)` y
`r sprintf("%.3f",ssb_f_loo_summary_wd$Spearman_max)` for Spearman.


```{r tab-assessment-parameters, results='asis'}
latex_table_fit(
  assessment_parameters,
  caption="Parameters estimated from the 20 annual SS3 revisions corresponding to 2005--2024.",
  label="tab:assessment-parameters",
  digits=3
)
```

The annual variation in log revisions is shown in
Figure \@ref(fig:fig-assessment-error-time).

```{r fig-assessment-error-time, out.width="75%", fig.cap="Annual log revisions of SSB, fishing mortality, and recruitment corresponding to the 2005--2024 updates. The dashed line represents zero error and the solid line the mean log revision for each variable."}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(fig_dir,"02_assessment_error_time_series.png"))
```

## Temporal structure {#results-temporal}

The first-order temporal-dependence coefficients were
\(\phi=`r sprintf("%.3f",assessment_temporal$phi[assessment_temporal$variable=="SSB"])`\)
para SSB,
\(\phi=`r sprintf("%.3f",assessment_temporal$phi[assessment_temporal$variable=="F"])`\)
para \(F\) y
\(\phi=`r sprintf("%.3f",assessment_temporal$phi[assessment_temporal$variable=="R"])`\)
for recruitment. The \(p\)-values were
`r sprintf("%.3f",assessment_temporal$p_value[assessment_temporal$variable=="SSB"])`,
`r sprintf("%.3f",assessment_temporal$p_value[assessment_temporal$variable=="F"])` y
`r sprintf("%.3f",assessment_temporal$p_value[assessment_temporal$variable=="R"])`,
respectively (Table \@ref(tab:assessment-temporal)).

The first-order temporal-dependence coefficients were
\(\phi=0.022\) para SSB, \(\phi=0.057\) para \(F\) y \(\phi=0.056\) para
reclutamiento, con valores de \(p\) de 0.930, 0.817 y 0.825,
respectively (Table \@ref(tab:assessment-temporal)). Con estos resultados,
el modelo de referencia se implementó con \(\phi=0\) para las tres variables.
La covariación contemporánea entre SSB, \(F\) y reclutamiento se mantuvo
mediante la matriz de varianzas--covarianzas \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}\).


```{r tab-assessment-temporal, results='asis'}
latex_table_fit(
  assessment_temporal,
  caption="First-order temporal-dependence coefficients estimated for annual revisions of SSB, fishing mortality, and recruitment.",
  label="tab:assessment-temporal",
  digits=3
)
```


## Internal validation {#results-internal-validation}

In the 10,000 realizations used to check implementation of the emulator, the
simulated means were
`r sprintf("%.3f",emulator_validation$simulated_mean[emulator_validation$variable=="SSB"])`,
`r sprintf("%.3f",emulator_validation$simulated_mean[emulator_validation$variable=="F"])`
y
`r sprintf("%.3f",emulator_validation$simulated_mean[emulator_validation$variable=="R"])`
for SSB, \(F\), and recruitment, respectively. The values used in the
parameterization were
`r sprintf("%.3f",emulator_validation$target_mean[emulator_validation$variable=="SSB"])`,
`r sprintf("%.3f",emulator_validation$target_mean[emulator_validation$variable=="F"])`
y
`r sprintf("%.3f",emulator_validation$target_mean[emulator_validation$variable=="R"])`.

The simulated standard deviations were
`r sprintf("%.3f",emulator_validation$simulated_sd[emulator_validation$variable=="SSB"])`,
`r sprintf("%.3f",emulator_validation$simulated_sd[emulator_validation$variable=="F"])`
y
`r sprintf("%.3f",emulator_validation$simulated_sd[emulator_validation$variable=="R"])`,
compared with parameterization values of
`r sprintf("%.3f",emulator_validation$target_sd[emulator_validation$variable=="SSB"])`,
`r sprintf("%.3f",emulator_validation$target_sd[emulator_validation$variable=="F"])`
y
`r sprintf("%.3f",emulator_validation$target_sd[emulator_validation$variable=="R"])`,
respectivamente.

The simulated correlations were
`r sprintf("%.3f",emulator_cor_wd["SSB","F"])` para SSB--\(F\),
`r sprintf("%.3f",emulator_cor_wd["SSB","R"])` para SSB--\(R\) y
`r sprintf("%.3f",emulator_cor_wd["F","R"])` para \(F\)--\(R\). The values
used in the parameterization were
`r sprintf("%.3f",assessment_par_rds$correlation["SSB","F"])`,
`r sprintf("%.3f",assessment_par_rds$correlation["SSB","R"])` y
`r sprintf("%.3f",assessment_par_rds$correlation["F","R"])`,
respectively (Table \@ref(tab:emulator-validation)).

## Validation using conventional retrospectives {#results-external-validation}

The observed retrospective errors for *peels* -1 to -5 were compared with the
distributions obtained from 10,000 simulated sequences. All 15 observed
errors, corresponding to five *peels* and three variables, fell within the
5th and 95th percentiles of the simulated distributions
(Table \@ref(tab:retrospective-validation)).

For SSB, observed errors ranged from -0.396 to 0.008; for \(F\), from -0.007
to 0.574; and for recruitment, from -0.304 to 0.363.

```{r tab-retrospective-validation, results='asis'}
retro_validation <- read.csv(
  file.path(tab_dir, "04_retrospective_validation.csv")
)

retro_validation_display <- retro_validation

names(retro_validation_display) <- c(
  "Peel",
  "Year",
  "Variable",
  "Observed",
  "Median",
  "p05",
  "p95",
  "Within 90%"
)

latex_table_fit(
  retro_validation_display,
  caption = "Observed retrospective error and simulated distribution for peels -1 to -5.",
  label = "tab:retrospective-validation",
  digits = 3
)
```

Observed Mohn's rho was -0.134 for SSB, 0.335 for \(F\), and 0.041 for
recruitment. All three values fell within the 5th and 95th percentiles of the
corresponding simulated distributions (Table \@ref(tab:mohn-validation)).

```{r tab-mohn-validation, results='asis'}
mohn_validation <- read.csv(
  file.path(tab_dir, "05_mohn_rho_validation.csv")
)

mohn_validation_display <- mohn_validation

names(mohn_validation_display) <- c(
  "Variable",
  "Observed rho",
  "Median",
  "p05",
  "p95",
  "Within 90%"
)

latex_table_fit(
  mohn_validation_display,
  caption = "Observed Mohn's rho and distribution obtained from 10,000 simulated sequences.",
  label = "tab:mohn-validation",
  digits = 3
)
```

Four of the five peels showed positive errors for \(F\), three for
recruitment, and one for SSB. The frequencies of these patterns in the 10,000
simulated sequences were 0.281, 0.702, and 0.288, respectively
(Table \@ref(tab:direction-validation)).

```{r tab-direction-validation, results='asis'}
direction_validation <- read.csv(
  file.path(tab_dir, "06_directional_validation.csv")
)

direction_validation_display <- direction_validation

names(direction_validation_display) <- c(
  "Variable",
  "Positive",
  "Negative",
  "Frequency"
)

latex_table_fit(
  direction_validation_display,
  caption = "Directional persistence of retrospective errors and corresponding frequency in simulated sequences.",
  label = "tab:direction-validation",
  digits = 3
)
```

The accumulated errors by peel, Mohn's rho, and directional persistence are
shown together in Figure
\@ref(fig:fig-external-validation).

```{r fig-external-validation, out.width="95%", fig.cap="Validation using conventional SS3 retrospectives. (A) Observed retrospective error by peel and median and 5th and 95th percentiles of simulations. (B) Observed Mohn's rho and simulated distribution. (C) Observed directional persistence and corresponding frequency under the simulated process."}
knitr::include_graphics(
  file.path(
    fig_dir,
    "05_assessment_error_external_validation.png"
  )
)
```

## Realizations used in the MSE {#results-mse-trajectories}

A total of 1,000 multivariate *assessment-error* realizations were generated
for assessment years 2024--2053. The final object contains 30 years, 1,000
iterations, and three variables: SSB, \(F\), and recruitment.

Checks of the final object confirmed the specified dimensions, the presence
of all three variables, and the absence of non-finite or non-positive
multipliers.

The object was stored as

`data/Rdata/assessment_error_reference_1000iter.rds`

and constitutes the *assessment-error* input subsequently used in the MSE
*closed-loop* simulations.

# Reproducibility {#reproducibility}

The *assessment-error* component is generated by the script
`14_build_assessment_error.R`. The script uses moving SS3 retrospectives with terminal years 2004--2024 to
calculate annual revisions and parameterize the emulator. Conventional
retrospectives with *peels* 0 to -5 are used for validation.

The script calculates historical revisions of SSB, \(F\), and recruitment,
estimates the parameters of the multivariate model, performs validation
diagnostics, and generates the 1,000 *assessment-error* realizations
subsequently used in the MSE.

The computational sequence is:

\[
\begin{aligned}
&\text{SS3 retrospectives} \\
&\downarrow \\
&\text{historical revisions} \\
&\downarrow \\
&\text{emulator parameterization and validation} \\
&\downarrow \\
&\texttt{assessment\_error\_reference\_1000iter.rds}
\end{aligned}
\]

The final object is stored in
`data/Rdata/assessment_error_reference_1000iter.rds`. The tables used
in this WD are stored in `outputs/assessment_error/tables/` and the figures in
`outputs/assessment_error/figures/`.

The R Markdown does not rerun SS3 or regenerate the *assessment-error*
realizations. Numerical results and figures are read from the outputs
generated by `14_build_assessment_error.R`, maintaining traceability among
code, outputs, and reported results.


# Conclusions

- Las historical revisions de SS3 mostraron diferencias en magnitud y dirección entre SSB, mortalidad por pesca y reclutamiento, con desviaciones estándar de 0.191, 0.284 y 0.310 en escala logarítmica, respectivamente.

- SSB and fishing-mortality revisions showed a negative correlation of -0.979, which was maintained in the *leave-one-year-out* analysis. This relationship was incorporated into the emulator through the variance--covariance matrix.

- The first-order temporal-dependence coefficients were próximos a cero para SSB, mortalidad por pesca y reclutamiento, sin evidencia estadística de dependencia temporal. El modelo de referencia se implementó con errores independientes entre años y mantuvo la dependencia entre variables dentro de cada año.

- Emulator simulations reproduced the means, standard deviations, and correlations used in its parameterization.

- Observed errors in the conventional retrospectives for *peels* -1 to -5 and Mohn's rho values fell within the 5th and 95th percentiles of the simulated distributions for all three variables.

- The results support use of the emulator as a representation of *assessment error* in the *shortcut MSE*. The 1,000 realizations generated for 2024--2053 provide the multipliers that will subsequently be applied to the state perceived by the Management Procedure.
